FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by 'the Indian Standards Institution on 27 April 1967, after the draft finalized by the Dairy Products and Laboratory Apparatus Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural
and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 IUSOGOLLA is a popular sweet prepared generally from cow milk and is a good. source of milk proteins. Milk is first boiled and curdled, uwally by adding an adequate quantity of whey. It is then filtered by IIIlring into a mull bag and the 'curd collected and. cooled by immersing the mull bag in cold water. When sufficiently cooled, the bag if taken out and the excess fluid gently squeezed. The sweet curd called' CHA.NNA. ' !s then ~eaded.to a.creamt consisten~y and made into small balls w~ch are Immediately boiled in previously clarified sugar syrup for about 10 mtDutes. IUS 0 GOLLAS, along wiih hot syrup, are filled in sterilized can~ The filled cans are immediately sealed and cooled. . 0.3 Keeping in view the considerable amount of intentate trade and export market of. RA.SOGOL~ quality control .. very essential"
'I

0.4 Preparation of this standard had been taken up on a requ$ from Development Council for FoOd Processing Industries, . ~,\' 0.5 While formulating this standard, necessary consideration h.. been given to the relevant rules prescribed by the Government of India under the Prevention of'-Food Adulteration Act, 1954. This standard is subiect to . restrictions imposed under that Act and the rules framed thereunder, wherever
applicable.

0.6 In the prepara~ion of this standard, assistance has been derived from the fo~lowing:

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value ~ should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
'1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of test for canned RASOGOLLA prepared from milk.

2. RE(lUIREMENTS
2.1 Canned RASOGOLLA shall be prepared from CHANNA obtained from clean, fresh and sweet milk. It shall be white or light creamy in colour. It shall be free from dirt and other foreign matter as well as insect and mould growth. It .shall be manufactured and packed under hygienic conditions as prescribed in IS : 2491.1963f.
,

2.2 RASOGOLLA to syrup ratio in the container shall be about 2 :'3 when determined by the method given-In J-33. . 2.3 The product shall also comply with the requirements given in Tables 1 and 2. '

.

3. PACKING, MARKING AND STORAGE
3.1 P-cJdas - The material shall be filled in sterilized sanitary, cans or any other suitable containen with as little air as possible.� The container should preclude contamination with metals or otlter impurities. 3.2 Muldal - Each container shall be marked leg'bly with t~e following information: a) Name of the product, b) Name and address of the manufacturer,
-Rules for rouDding offnumericaJ valun (MJisld). tCode for IaIlitary ~ODditioDi for rood procadDl unlu.

4

II, 4.071. IN7
c) Net weight of the contents in the container in grams, d) Batch or code number, and e) A statement to the effect that the material should be kept in � cool place.
3.2.1 The product may also be marked witb Standard mlrk. 3.2.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by tbe provisions of tbe Bureau o/Indian Standards Act, 1986 and tbe Rules .nd Regulltions made thereunder, The details of conditions under wbicb tbe licence for tbe use of Standard Mark may be grinted to manufacturers or producen may be obtained from tbe Bureau of Indian Standards.

APPENDIX J ( Clause S.1 )
SAMPLING 0 .. RASOGOLLJf J-l. GENERAL UQ,'VIREMENTS
J-l.0 In drawing t preparing, storing and handling the samples, the followmg precautions and directions shall be observed. J-1.1 The sampling instrument shall be clean and

dry when used.

J-l.2 Precautions shall be taken to, protect the samples, the materials being sampled, the sampling instrument and the containen from adventitious contamination. J-l.3 Sampling shall be done by a penon agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor and, if desired by either of them, in the presence of the purchaser (o~ his representative) and the vendor ( or his representative ). J-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING J-4.1 Lot - All the containers in a single consignment of the material Clrawn from a lingle batch of manufacture shall constitute a Jot. If a consignment is declared or known to cOf\lilt of different batches of manufacture, 1he containen belonging to the same batch shall be grouped together and each group shall constitute a separate lot.

J-2.1.1 Samplea shall be tested for each lot ascertaining t.he conformity of the material to the requirements of this standard.
J-2.2 The number n of containers to be selected from the lot shall depend on the size �\' of the lot and shall be as given in Table 3.

J-2.3 These containers \ shall be selected at random from the lot and, to ensure the randomnelf of selection, a random number table as agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor shall be used. Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn from the lot to give a sample for test where r == N In, N being the size of the lot and n the number of containers to be selected (sel Table 3 ). In case r comes to be a fractional number, its value shan be taken as equal to the integral part of it.
J-3. TEST SAMPLES AND REFEREE S~PLE J-3.1 The containers selected as in J-2.2 shall be divided at random ii\to three equal sets and labelled with all the particulars of sampling.
